Reviewer: m3 pool job review-4423, Claude Fable 5.2 (claude-fable-5-2), mkinney seat (`.claude-mkinney`); did not write or refresh this PR.

**Needs changes before merge.** This is a SAFETY-tier review: the PR changes posted G-code and the verification gate. This is the first review. It lists each finding of the whole diff.

Ownership record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4423#issuecomment-7227191499

## What is good

- The two new goldens are correct, line by line. Each copy has the shift that the pattern gives. Z, feeds and tool numbers do not change. The by-tool program has 3 tool changes. The by-part program has 7 sections in the order Face1, then (Face2, Face3) at copies 1, 2 and 3.
- `cl::transform::copies` is in the `cl` crate and has its own tests. The link never goes below the end or the start of a path.
- Each command validates at creation and each has an undo. The MCP tools call the same commands.
- A turned or flipped WCS, a tilted move, a probe and a broken row order are refused by name.
- The body has `Process change: yes`, a `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #3012` and a decisions file. The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. The PR adds no dependency. The PR changes no `crates/ui` file, thus no screenshots are necessary.

## Results (local, trial merge with `upstream/main` `392980120`, merge `927250854`)

The host is `m3`. No GitHub runner was used. The trial merge has no conflict.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-app --no-run` | builds |
| Pins: `pattern_folder::*`, `pattern_folder_post::*` (8 tests, `mcp` suite) | 8 passed |
| Pins: `cl::transform::copies::tests::*` | 6 passed |
| `cl suites` (lib, edge_volume, headless_bin, origin_approach, refusal_log) | 5 of 5 green |
| `app suites: lib` | green |
| `app suites: mcp` | green |
| `app suites: example_catalog` | green (see the note) |
| All 709 `app suites` steps of the plan (`gate batch --lane 1/3`, `2/3`, `3/3`, `--only "app suites"`) | 708 green, 1 red under load, green when run again |
| `clippy -D warnings` (the gate step, all crates) | green |
| `cargo xtask gate light` | 6 of 6 green (9.4 min) |

Note on the red step: in lane 1, `app suites: example_catalog` failed two tests, `catalog_3d_rough_finish::rebuilds` and `::regenerates`. The log shows `elapsed=60.000s budget=60.000s`. This is the 60 s debug time budget, with 8 lanes on the host. The output has no difference in content. The same step was green before that run (79 s) and after it (20 s, alone). The case has no pattern folder. I do not count it as a failure of this PR.

Not run by me: the `motion`, `post`, `sim`, `geometry`, `gcode`, `tools`, `kernel`, `gpu`, `ui-kit` and `ui` steps of the fallback batch plan (the `cl` change makes the quick tier fall back to 1235 steps). The `cl` change only adds a module and one `pub use` line. The heavy lanes were not run (P6, AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review"). No heavy record names this head.

Extra suites run:
- Test data: the PR adds two files in `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/pattern_folder/`. The suites that read the golden directory are `mcp` (the two pins), `solid_law_goldens` and `golden_cl`. All three are green.
- Importers: the diff does not touch import code. The kernel STEP suites were not necessary.

## Mutations (run by me)

| Mutation | Pins |
|---|---|
| `enabled_offsets` ignores `disabled_instances` (`pattern_folder.rs`) | RED: the two goldens, the by-part section count, the `enabled_offsets` assert |
| The row-law refusal is off (`posting_pattern.rs`, `if !together`) | RED: `a_folder_the_post_cannot_write_refuses_by_name` |
| The link plane is `link_z` only (`transform_copies.rs`) | RED: `a_low_link_plane_never_dips_below_the_path_ends` |
| The after-action and the setup-change stop go on each by-part section (`posting.rs:1321`, `posting.rs:1361`) | GREEN: no pin fails (finding 3) |
| `pattern_problems` judges no folder (`posting_pattern.rs:146`) | GREEN: no pin fails (finding 3) |

The tree was restored after each mutation.

## Requested before merge

Each finding names its class. Please close the class with one rule, not only the one case.

1. **A pattern folder is counted as a model.** Class: a new row kind is not excluded from a kind test.
   `crates/app/src/model.rs:163` (`is_model`) excludes stock, WCS, tools, operations, setups, entries (#155) and sketches (#1862). It does not exclude a pattern folder. Measured on this head: after `create_pattern_folder`, `model::model_entities` gives `["Pattern1"]` on a document with no model, and `get_job` gives `"models": [{"bounds":null,"facets":0,"fixture":false,"name":"Pattern1"}]`.
   The effect is not only the list. These laws read `model_entities` or `is_model` to decide if the document has a part: `stock_source.rs:193`, `sketch_model.rs:52`, `operation/wire_sketch.rs:108`, `stock_fit.rs`, `setup_align.rs`, `stock_sim.rs:450`. The UI model list and `TagFixture` also accept the folder as a model.
   Fix: add `&& !crate::pattern_folder::is_pattern(world, entity)` to `is_model`. Add a pin: with a folder in the document, `model_entities` and the `models` of `get_job` do not change.

2. **A project file that names one operation in two folders posts wrong G-code.** Class: the load does not check the membership law, and the plan trusts a count.
   - `crates/app/src/project/pattern_dto.rs:94` (`validate`) checks one folder at a time. It does not refuse a member that a second folder names. The commands refuse this (`checked_members`), but a file can state it.
   - `crates/app/src/posting_pattern.rs:109`: `owner.insert` lets the last folder win, without a refusal.
   - `crates/app/src/posting_pattern.rs:120`: `ops.iter().skip(i).take(posted.len())` takes the next N operations by count. It does not check that they are the folder's members.
   Measured on this head (a probe test, not committed): rows `Pattern1, Face1, Face2, Pattern2, Face3, Face4`, with `Pattern1` = [Face1, Face2] and `Pattern2` = [Face2, Face3]. `verification_report` gives no problem. The Fanuc program posts **Face4, which is in no folder, a second time at Y+200** (the shift of `Pattern2`). Face2 posts with the shift of `Pattern1`.
   This is degenerate input that gives wrong output with no diagnostic (Prime Directive).
   Fix, the two parts:
   - At load, refuse a file where one operation is a member of two folders. Refuse a member that is not an operation of the file.
   - In `plan` (and thus in `pattern_problems`), refuse by name when a member already has an owner. Take the members by name, not by count.
   Add a pin for each part.

3. **Two safety laws of this PR have no pin.** Class: behaviour that the body states, and that no test fails for.
   - The by-part law "the after-action and the setup-change stop go only on the last section of each operation" (`crates/app/src/posting.rs:1321`, `:1361`). With the guard removed, all 8 pins are green. Without the guard, an `M0` or a setup-change stop posts after each copy. Add a by-part pin with an after-action (a Pause entry or `op.after`) on a member, and assert that the stop is in the program one time, after the last copy.
   - The copy gate, `pattern_problems` (`crates/app/src/posting_pattern.rs:146`). With the gate off, all 8 pins are green. The gate works: in my probe a fixture in the area of copy 2 blocks the post with `Face1 copy 2 (Pattern1): shank at move 2 strikes a fixture`. But no test keeps it. Add one pin where a copy strikes a fixture and one pin where a copy leaves the machine travel. Assert that the post is blocked with the folder name and the copy number, and that the post is clear when that copy is turned off.

## Optional, not blocking

- `crates/app/src/mcp/pattern_tools.rs:105`: `dir` uses `filter_map(Value::as_f64)`. `"dir": [1, "x", 0]` becomes `[1, 0]` and is accepted. Refuse an entry that is not a number.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp/pattern_folder_post.rs:59`: the assert "copy 2 is not cut" cannot fail. The X values of copy 2 are 20, 22, 58 and 60, and the range is 25 to 55. The golden catches the mutation, so the law is pinned. A range of 19 to 61 makes the assert true to its text.
- `crates/cl/src/cl/transform_copies.rs:47` returns `TransformError::TiltedMove`. Its text (`transform.rs:87`) says "cannot be mirrored". For a copy, the user reads the wrong word.
- The not-judged line says that the other copies "are checked for machine travel and fixtures". The link rapid between two copies (by tool) is not part of that check: `pattern_problems` judges each copy alone. I found no unsafe case: the first-rapid law refuses a clearance height below a fixture top (my probe with a 60 mm fixture between the copies was refused by that law), and the link is at the clearance height or above. #3013 already lists "every inter-copy clearance rapid link". Please add this to "Not exercised" in the body.
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs` has 1701 lines and grows by 16. It was above 400 lines before this PR.

## Labels and state

- `needs-rework` is set. The PR is `MERGEABLE` and stays a draft.
- A `feat` PR merges at the cut.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: the three findings of the review of `eaa90f1d6`, and two of the optional remarks. The new head is `07cd14690ab03f863484a6dc3086ac2927a9f115`.

Writer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3012#issuecomment-7228096704

All new pins are in `crates/app/tests/mcp/pattern_folder_law.rs` (`mcp` directory suite).

**1. A pattern folder is counted as a model.**
- `model::is_model` now excludes a pattern folder. This is the one kind test, thus each reader of `is_model` and `model_entities` gets the rule.
- Pin: `pattern_folder_law::a_folder_is_not_a_model`. With a folder in the document, `model_entities` and the `models` of `get_job` do not change.
- Mutation: without the clause, the pin is red.

**2. A project file that names one operation in two folders.**
- Load: `pattern_dto::validate_members` checks the whole file before any world write. It refuses a member that is not an operation row of the file. It refuses an operation that two folders name, with the operation and the two folders in the message.
- Post: `refusal` in `posting_pattern.rs` refuses by name a member that a second active folder names. `plan` and `pattern_problems` use the same function. `plan` takes the members by name.
- Pins: `pattern_folder_law::a_file_breaking_the_membership_law_is_refused_at_load` and `pattern_folder_law::two_folders_that_name_one_operation_refuse_the_post_by_name`.
- Mutations: without the load check, the first pin is red. Without the second-owner check, the second pin is red.
- Not pinned alone: "by name, not by count". The row-law refusal and the second-owner refusal make the two forms equal, thus no test can see the difference.

**3. Two safety laws had no pin.**
- By-part after-action: `pattern_folder_law::a_by_part_stop_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy`. Face2 has a program stop and is cut at 3 copies. The program has one `M0`, between tool change 6 and tool change 7.
- By-part setup change: `pattern_folder_law::a_by_part_setup_change_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy`. The stream has one `SetupChange` and the program has one `M0`, after the last copy.
- Copy gate, fixture: `pattern_folder_law::a_copy_that_strikes_a_fixture_blocks_the_post_until_it_is_off`. The gate and the post say `Face1 copy 2 (Pattern1): ... strikes a fixture`. The gate is clear when copy 2 is off.
- Copy gate, travel: `pattern_folder_law::a_copy_outside_the_machine_travel_blocks_the_post_until_it_is_off`. The gate and the post name `Face1 copy 3 (Pattern1)`. The gate is clear when copy 3 is off.
- Mutations: the guard at `posting.rs:1321` removed gives the two by-part pins red. The guard at `posting.rs:1361` removed gives the setup-change pin red. `pattern_problems` with no judgement gives the fixture pin and the travel pin red.

**Optional remarks.**
- Done: the MCP `dir` refuses an entry that is not a number (pinned in `a_folder_is_not_a_model`, red without the fix).
- Done: the "copy 2 is not cut" assert. The range 19 to 61 from the review also holds X 20 of copy 1 and X 60 of copy 3, thus the assert uses 21 to 59. It is red when `enabled_offsets` ignores `disabled_instances`.
- Done: the body says under "Not exercised" that the link rapid between copies is not part of the copy gate.
- Not done: the text of `TransformError::TiltedMove`, and the length of `posting.rs`.

**Gate on `07cd14690`, against `upstream/main` `4d891498e`.**
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 1231 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. This includes `clippy -D warnings` and the three `example_catalog*` suites.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 of 6 steps pass.
- No golden changed.

Please review the new head again.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge (at the cut: this is a `feat`).** This is a SAFETY-tier re-review: the PR changes posted G-code and the verification gate. The earlier review was on `eaa90f1d6`. The fix commit `07cd14690` closes each of its findings.

Ownership record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4423#issuecomment-7228797315

## Earlier findings (review of `eaa90f1d6`)

1. **A pattern folder is counted as a model.** Fixed. `model::is_model` excludes a folder (`crates/app/src/model.rs:171`). Each reader of `is_model` and `model_entities` gets the rule. Pin: `pattern_folder_law::a_folder_is_not_a_model`. My mutation (clause removed): the pin is red.
2. **A file that names one operation in two folders posts wrong G-code.** Fixed, the two parts:
   - Load: `pattern_dto::validate_members` runs in `check_and_apply` before any world write. It refuses a member that is not an operation row of the file, and an operation in two folders. Pin: `a_file_breaking_the_membership_law_is_refused_at_load`. My mutation (the call removed): the pin is red.
   - Post: `refusal` refuses a member that a second active folder names. `plan` and `pattern_problems` use the same function. `plan` takes the members by name and writes each folder once (`written`). Pin: `two_folders_that_name_one_operation_refuse_the_post_by_name`. My mutation (the second-owner loop off): the pin is red.
3. **Two safety laws have no pin.** Fixed.
   - By-part after-action and setup change: `a_by_part_stop_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy` and `a_by_part_setup_change_is_written_once_after_the_last_copy`. My mutation (the after-action on each section, `posting.rs:1321`): the two pins are red.
   - Copy gate: `a_copy_that_strikes_a_fixture_blocks_the_post_until_it_is_off` and `a_copy_outside_the_machine_travel_blocks_the_post_until_it_is_off`. Each asserts the gate line, the post refusal with the folder and copy number, and a clear gate when that copy is off. My mutation (`pattern_problems` judges no copy): the two pins are red.

The optional remarks: `dir` now refuses an entry that is not a number (pinned). The "copy 2 is not cut" assert uses 21 to 59 and can fail. The body now says that the link rapid between copies is not part of the copy gate. The `TiltedMove` text and the length of `posting.rs` are not changed. They stay optional.

The new test file `crates/app/tests/mcp/pattern_folder_law.rs` is in the `mcp` directory suite. It is not a new test binary.

The `cl` change of the first commit only adds a module and one `pub use` line. The author ran the full quick plan (1231 steps, 0 failed) on this head against `4d891498e`. The heavy lanes were not run: this is a P6 PR (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").

Extra suites run:
- Test data: the fix commit changes no golden and no test data. The suites that read `crates/app/tests/golden/` (`mcp`, `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens`) are green.
- Importers: the diff does not touch import code. The kernel STEP suites were not necessary.

## Mutations (run by me on this head)

| Mutation | Pins |
|---|---|
| The after-action goes on each by-part section (`posting.rs:1321`) | RED: `a_by_part_stop_...`, `a_by_part_setup_change_...` |

The tree was restored after each mutation. With the tree restored, 15 of 15 pins pass.

## Law check

- Goldens: no golden moved in the fix commit. The two new goldens of the first commit are listed under "Goldens moved". The earlier review read them line by line.
- Process: the body has `Process change: yes`. The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`. The body has a `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #3012`.
- The PR changes no `crates/ui` file, thus no screenshots are necessary.
- The PR adds no dependency and no `camcraft-*` edge.
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` in the new non-test code of the fix commit.

None.
